verdict.rationale: LiteLLM's proxy docs say it logs proxy input, output and exceptions to many destinations a developer can own. These include OpenTelemetry, S3/GCS/Azure buckets, DataDog, Langfuse, Langsmith, SQS and custom callbacks to your own API endpoints. Each request also gets a unique call_id for tracing it across the system. missing for 10: independent or hands-on confirmation that the exports work, and deeper documentation of what the trace/span data contains (the OpenTelemetry export is only listed by name).

support.subject: As a developer, I can export gateway logs and traces to my own observability stack

citations.quote: Log Proxy input, output, and exceptions using: Langfuse OpenTelemetry GCS, s3, Azure (Blob) Buckets AWS SQS Lunary MLflow Deepeval Custom Callbacks - Custom code and API endpoints Langsmith DataDog Azure Sentinel DynamoDB
LiteLLM generates a unique call_id for each request. This call_id can be used to track the request across the system.
This will prevent the messages and responses from being logged to your logging provider, but request metadata - e.g. spend, will still be tracked.
